importantNotes: Elisha performed twice as many miracles as Elijah — he received a double portion.
Israel (the Northern Kingdom) fell to Assyria in 722 BC and never returned.
Josiah's revival (chs. 22-23) was the last great spiritual reform before the exile.
The Babylonian exile fulfilled Jeremiah's prophecy of 70 years of captivity.
The book shows that disobedience leads to judgment, but God always preserves a remnant.

chapters.1: Elijah calls fire from heaven on the soldiers sent by King Ahaziah.
chapters.2: Elijah is taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire; Elisha receives a double portion.
chapters.3: Israel, Judah, and Edom unite against Moab; Elisha provides water and victory.
chapters.4: Elisha's miracles — widow's oil multiplied, the Shunammite's son raised from death.
chapters.5: Naaman the Syrian commander is healed of leprosy; Gehazi's greed is punished.
chapters.6: The floating axe head; Elisha's supernatural intelligence helps Israel against Syria.
chapters.7: Four lepers discover the Aramean army has fled; the siege of Samaria ends.
chapters.8: The Shunammite woman's land restored; Hazael becomes king of Aram; kings of Judah.
chapters.9: Jehu is anointed king of Israel; he kills Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel.
chapters.10: Jehu destroys Ahab's family and the worshippers of Baal.
chapters.11: Athaliah usurps the throne of Judah; Joash is hidden and later crowned as king.
chapters.12: King Joash repairs the Temple; Hazael threatens Jerusalem; Joash is assassinated.
chapters.13: Kings Jehoahaz and Jehoash of Israel; Elisha's death and final miracle.
chapters.14: King Amaziah of Judah; King Jeroboam II of Israel expands the northern kingdom.
chapters.15: A succession of kings in Israel and Judah; Assyria begins to threaten Israel.
chapters.16: King Ahaz of Judah seeks help from Assyria; he introduces pagan worship in the Temple.
chapters.17: The fall of Israel (Samaria) to Assyria in 722 BC; the reasons for the exile.
chapters.18: King Hezekiah's faithful reign; Assyria invades Judah and threatens Jerusalem.
chapters.19: Hezekiah prays; Isaiah prophesies deliverance; an angel destroys 185,000 Assyrians.
chapters.20: Hezekiah's illness and miraculous recovery; he foolishly shows his treasures to Babylon.
chapters.21: King Manasseh's wicked reign — the worst king of Judah; Amon follows his evil ways.
chapters.22: King Josiah discovers the Book of the Law; Huldah the prophetess confirms God's judgment.
chapters.23: Josiah's great reform — he destroys idols, altars, and renews the covenant; Josiah dies in battle.
chapters.24: Babylon invades Judah; King Jehoiachin is taken captive; Zedekiah is installed.
chapters.25: Jerusalem and the Temple are destroyed by Babylon in 586 BC; the people go into exile.
